name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
definition: A long-term condition where the kidneys gradually lose their function over time, typically measured by a decline in the Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR).
symptoms: Change in urination frequency, especially at night
treatment: Strict management of blood pressure and blood sugar
Medications (e.g., ACE inhibitors or ARBs) to slow progression
Dietary changes (low salt, controlled protein intake)
Dialysis or kidney transplant in late-stage failure
prevention: Regular monitoring of blood pressure and blood sugar
Maintaining a healthy weight and diet
Avoiding overuse of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

name: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI)
definition: A sudden, rapid decrease in kidney function that develops over hours or days, often reversible if treated promptly.
symptoms: Fluid retention, causing swelling in legs
causes: Blockage of the urinary tract (e.g., severe kidney stones)
diagnosis: Rapid increase in serum creatinine and BUN
treatment: Treating the underlying cause (e.g., fighting infection, restoring fluid balance)
Temporary dialysis if fluid/electrolyte levels are critical
prevention: Maintaining adequate hydration, especially when ill
Careful monitoring of medications in high-risk patients

name: Kidney Stones (Nephrolithiasis)
definition: Hard deposits made of minerals and salts that form inside the kidneys, often causing severe pain as they travel through the urinary tract.
symptoms: Severe, sharp pain in the side and back (flank pain)
Pain that radiates to the lower abdomen and groin
causes: High intake of salt, sugar, and animal protein
treatment: Increased fluid intake and pain management for small stones
Medications to help pass the stone
Shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) for breaking stones
Ureteroscopy or surgery for large stones
prevention: Drinking plenty of water (2.5L-3L per day)
Reducing salt and high-oxalate foods (e.g., spinach, nuts)

name: Diabetic Nephropathy
definition: A complication of long-term diabetes, where high blood sugar damages the small filtering units in the kidneys (glomeruli), leading to kidney failure.
symptoms: Foamy or bubbly urine due to excessive protein (albuminuria)
Swelling in the feet, ankles, and hands
Increased need to urinate at night
High blood pressure that is difficult to control
causes: Long duration of diabetes (Type 1 or Type 2)
diagnosis: Blood tests for eGFR and creatinine
treatment: Achieving strict blood glucose control (HbA1c targets)
Aggressive blood pressure control using ACE inhibitors or ARBs
Dietary management (low salt and controlled protein)
prevention: Regular monitoring and strict control of blood sugar
Maintaining blood pressure within recommended targets

name: Pyelonephritis (Kidney Infection)
definition: A bacterial infection of the kidney, often starting as a Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) that travels up to the kidney.
symptoms: Severe pain in the back or side (flank pain)
causes: Bacterial infection (E. coli most common) ascending from the bladder
Obstruction in the urinary tract (e.g., stones or enlarged prostate)
diagnosis: Blood tests (checking for elevated white blood cells)
Ultrasound or CT scan if obstruction is suspected
treatment: Antibiotics (often intravenously initially for severe cases)
prevention: Prompt and complete treatment of lower UTIs
